findings.title: retryCount cleanup deletes reminders of every method, not just SMS
findings.body: The second branch of the deleteMany OR (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, unlike the first branch. Any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders that this SMS cron never touches, will be hard-deleted on every run. The condition should be scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` as well.

findings.title: Retry increment uses a stale in-memory value instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` writes a value read earlier in the run. If another worker or run updates the same row concurrently, one increment can be lost, so the row may survive longer than the intended two-failure limit. Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }` would avoid this.

findings.title: Unguarded DB update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (for example the row was deleted by a concurrent run), the exception escapes the for-loop and every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped, and the handler returns an error instead of `SMS scheduled`.

findings.title: Reminders with missing workflowStep/booking or empty message never accrue retries
findings.body: When `!reminder.workflowStep || !reminder.booking` the loop `continue`s without incrementing retryCount, and when the message is empty or sendTo is missing the `if (message?.length ...)` block is skipped, so no retry is recorded. Such rows stay unscheduled and are never cleaned up by the new retry-based deletion, so they are retried indefinitely on every cron run, which is the behavior this PR is meant to stop.
